full_text_zh:
[P1] 小老鼠麦克斯和几个小伙伴一起在草地上踢球，
突然，
爱捣乱的睡鼠瑞可跳出来，把球抢走了。
小伙伴们气坏了，
气势汹汹地要找瑞可去算账！
瑞可是不是再也不能成为大家的朋友了呢？

爱捣乱的瑞可

不受欢迎的小伙伴真的那么讨厌吗？
[奥]布丽吉特·威宁格 著 [法]伊芙·德勒 绘
杨玲玲 彭懿 译

德国
国宝级
儿童绘本

遇见美好 系列

[P2] 小老鼠麦克斯正和小伙伴们在草地上开心地玩儿呢。
“看球！莫莉，球飞到你那儿啦！”小黑鸟贝琳达喊道，她
不得不提醒着点儿，因为小鼹鼠莫莉的眼神儿不太好。
可这时，莫莉好像发现了什么，她抬起头，仔细瞅了瞅，又
闻了闻，说：“谁？还有谁在这儿？”
于是，大伙儿都朝四周张望起来。

[P3] “哦，不！是睡鼠瑞可！”小刺猬亨利小声说，他的神情很紧张。
“他一定是来捣乱的！”小黑鸟贝琳达说。
“睡鼠瑞可从来都不友好。”青蛙弗雷迪说着，偷偷地瞄了一眼那个黑影。
“大家都别理他。”贝琳达说。
“不管他，”麦克斯说，“咱们接着玩儿！”
麦克斯摆好球，瞄准，抬起自己的那条小短腿，一脚把球踢了出去。

[P4] 嗖——球朝灌木丛飞了过来。
瑞可像闪电一样冲了过去。他跳起来，一把接住球，逃跑了。
“喂！把球还给我们！”几个小伙伴大喊。
但是，瑞可丝毫没有停下来的意思，头也不回地跑了。
麦克斯气得都快说不出话了：“他怎么能这样呢！”
“真是太可恶了！”贝琳达说，“我就知道他是来捣乱的！”
“发……发生了什……什么事？”弗雷迪一脸困惑地问。

[P5] “我想，我能找到他。” 莫莉说着，上闻闻，下嗅嗅。
贝琳达可气坏了：“等咱们找到他，有他好看的！
不一会儿，他们发现了一个黑漆漆的洞口。
“这儿就是瑞可的家。” 莫莉小声地说。
“咱们现在该怎么办？” 麦克斯问。
“咱们得把球要回来！” 贝琳达说，“弗雷迪，快过来呀！”

[P6] “咚咚咚！”贝琳达用嘴使劲儿地敲门，“快点儿出来！把球还给我们！
“呱呱！”弗雷迪应和着。
可是，没人来开门。
“或许家里没人。”亨利说，“恐怕咱们得明天再来了。”
他们越想越生气，可一点儿办法也没有。

[P7] 过了一会儿，他们坐下来，一起商量该怎么办。
“瑞可那家伙总是捣乱，害得大家都没法玩儿了。”贝琳达说道。
“为什么呀？呱呱！为什么他要这么做呀？”弗雷迪问。
“我也不知道。”贝琳达还在气头上。
“要不，咱们请狐狸来帮帮忙，”亨利说，“他可是森林里最强壮的动物。”
“狐狸才懒得关心咱们的球呢，”莫莉说，“不行，明天咱们再过来，自己把球要回来！”
只有麦克斯什么都没说，他一直在安静地思考。

[P8] 第二天，他们又来到了瑞可家门口。
这回，莫莉和亨利自告奋勇，冲上前去敲门。
瑞可的妈妈开了门，问道：“你们是谁呀？”
“嗯……呃……那个……那个……可不可以把球还给我们呢？”
莫莉和亨利结结巴巴地说，“昨天，瑞可抢走了我们的球。”
瑞可的妈妈很生气，转身走进洞里。
“瑞可！”她吼道。
五个小伙伴直愣愣地站在那儿，不知该如何是好。

[P9] 突然，有个东西顺着又黑又长的走廊朝他们滚了过来。
“是咱们的球！”几个小伙伴大喊。
麦克斯一把抓住球，接得紧紧的。
“快走吧，我们一分钟都不想多待了。”几个小伙伴齐声说。
但麦克斯还站在那儿，一副若有所思的样子。
忽然，他好像知道自己该怎么做了……

[P10] 麦克斯把球往里一扔，球又顺着那条走廊滚了回去。
“嗨！瑞可！”他喊道，“你为什么不出来跟我们一起玩儿呢？
我们就在那边的草地上，你带上球一起来吧！”
其他几个小伙伴呆住了。他们看着麦克斯，不敢相信自己的耳朵。
“你疯了吗，麦克斯？”贝琳达说，“你明明知道他不会来的，
而且咱们的球再也要不回来了！”
“永——远——回
不来啦！”弗雷迪说。
“谁知道呢？”
麦克斯高兴地吹
着口哨，一瘸一拐
地向草地走去。

[P11] 果然，瑞可出来了。他手里还拿着球，正准备出发呢。
“太棒啦！你能来真好！”麦克斯说，“不能玩球可真是有点儿无聊呢。你想和我们一起玩儿吗？不过，玩儿的时候大家都得多留心，因为莫莉的眼神不太好，弗雷迪的耳朵不太灵，而我的腿跑不快。你还愿意和我们一起玩儿吗？”

[P12] 瑞可想了一会儿，点了点头。
“我的劲儿可大了。”他对这些新朋友说，“要不，我当守门员吧，这样就不会把大家撞倒了。”
“好主意！”麦克斯说，“咱们走！”
几个小伙伴玩儿啊，玩儿啊，一直玩儿到天都黑了。
瑞可最后一次接住了球，问：“对了，这是谁的球呀？”

[P13] “是咱们大家的！”五个小伙伴说。
“那就是说，它也是我的啦？”瑞可乐坏了，
“今天晚上我可以把它带回家吗？”
“当然可以啦！”麦克斯说，“只要大家学会分享，
一个球就够啦！”

full_text_en:
[P1] Little mouse Max and a few friends were playing soccer on the grass.
Suddenly,
the mischievous dormouse Rico jumped out and took the ball.
The friends were furious,
and stormed off to find Rico for a reckoning!
Would Rico ever be able to be everyone's friend again?

The Mischievous Rico

Are unpopular friends really so annoying?
[Aut] Brigitta Weining, author [Fr] Eve Deller, illustrator
Yang Lingling, Peng Yi, translators

Germany
National Treasure-level
Children's Picture Book

Meet Beauty Series

Tiger Exclusive Resource

[P2] Little mouse Max was playing happily with his friends on the grass.
"Look! Molly, the ball flew to you!" chirped the little blackbird Belinda, who had to remind everyone, because the little mole Molly had poor eyesight.
But then, Molly seemed to notice something. She lifted her head, looked carefully, sniffed, and said, "Who? Is someone else here?"
So everyone looked around.

[P3] "Oh, no! It's the dormouse Rico!" whispered Henry the hedgehog, his expression tense.
"He must be here to cause trouble!" said the little blackbird Belinda.
"Dormouse Rico is never friendly," said frog Freddy, secretly glancing at the dark shadow.
"Let's all ignore him," said Belinda.
"Don't mind him," said Max, "let's keep playing!"
Max positioned the ball, aimed, lifted his little short leg, and kicked the ball out with one foot.

[P4] Whoosh—the ball flew toward the bushes.
Rico dashed over like lightning. He jumped up, caught the ball, and ran away.
"Hey! Give the ball back to us!" the friends shouted.
But Rico didn't stop for a second, running off without looking back.
Max was so angry he could hardly speak: "How could he do that!"
"That's so terrible!" Belinda said, "I knew he was here to cause trouble!"
"Wha... what... what happened?" Freddy asked, looking confused.

[P5] "I think I can find him," Molly said, sniffing up and down.
Bella was furious: "When we find him, he's going to get it!"
Soon, they discovered a dark, dark hole.
"This is Riko's home," Molly whispered.
"What should we do now?" Max asked.
"We have to get the ball back!" Bella said, "Freddy, come quickly!"

[P6] "Knock, knock, knock!" Belinda knocked hard with her beak, "Come out! Give us back the ball!"
"Quack, quack!" Freddy echoed.
But no one came to open the door.
"Maybe no one is home," Henry said, "I guess we'll have to come back tomorrow."
They got angrier and angrier, but they had no idea what to do.

[P7] After a while, they sat down together to discuss what to do.
"Rico is always causing trouble, making it impossible for us to play," said Belinda.
"Why? Quack! Why would he do that?" asked Freddy.
"I don't know," Belinda said, still upset.
"What if we ask the fox for help?" said Henry. "He's the strongest animal in the forest."
"The fox wouldn't care about our ball," said Molly. "No, we'll come back tomorrow and get it back ourselves!"
Max said nothing. He was quietly thinking.

[P8] The next day, they came back to Riko's doorstep.
This time, Molly and Henry volunteered, rushing forward to knock on the door.
Riko's mom opened the door and asked, "Who are you?"
"Um... uh... that... that... can you please return the ball to us?"
Molly and Henry stammered, "Yesterday, Riko took our ball."
Riko's mom got very angry and turned to go back into the hole.
"Riko!" she shouted.
The five friends stood there, frozen, not knowing what to do.

[P9] Suddenly, something rolled down the long, dark corridor toward them.
“Our ball!” the friends shouted.
Max grabbed the ball tightly.
"Let's go, we don't want to stay one minute longer," the friends said together.
But Max still stood there, looking thoughtful.
Suddenly, he seemed to know what to do...

[P10] Max threw the ball inside, and it rolled back down the corridor.
"Hi, Rick!" he called out, "Why don't you come out and play with us?
We're over on the grass there. Bring the ball and come along!"
The other friends froze. They stared at Max, unable to believe their ears.
"Are you crazy, Max?" said Belinda. "You know he won't come,
and our ball will never come back!"
"Forever—never—coming
back!" said Freddy.
"Who knows?"
Max happily whistled,
limping off toward the grass.

[P11] Sure enough, Riko came out. He was still holding the ball, ready to set off.
"Great! It's so good you're here!" said Max. "It's really a bit boring not being able to play with the ball. Would you like to play with us? But we all need to be careful while playing, because Molly's eyesight isn't very good, Freddy's ears aren't very sharp, and my legs aren't fast. Would you still like to play with us?"

[P12] Riko thought for a moment and nodded.
"My strength is great," he said to his new friends. "Why don't I be the goalkeeper? That way, I won't knock anyone over."
"Good idea!" said Max. "Let's go!"
A few companions played and played until it got dark.
Riko caught the ball for the last time and asked, "By the way, whose ball is this?"

[P13] "It's ours all together!" the five friends said.
"That means it's mine too?" Rek was delighted,
"Can I take it home tonight?"
"Of course you can!" said Max, "As long as everyone learns to share,
One ball is enough!"

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页展示了绘本《爱捣乱的瑞可》的封面及内页文字，描述了小老鼠麦克斯和朋友们在草地上踢球时，被爱捣乱的睡鼠瑞可抢走球，朋友们因此生气并打算去找瑞可算账，引发对瑞可是否还能成为朋友的疑问。
[P2] 小老鼠麦克斯和朋友们在草地上玩耍时，小鼹鼠莫莉突然察觉到周围有异常，大家因此纷纷张望四周，似乎发现了什么不寻常的存在。
[P3] 朋友们发现睡鼠瑞可出现，纷纷认为他来捣乱并表示不满，但麦克斯选择无视他，继续踢球。
[P4] 瑞可抢走朋友们的球并逃跑，大家愤怒地喊叫，麦克斯气愤不已，贝琳达认为瑞可故意捣乱，而弗雷迪则一脸困惑。
[P5] 朋友们在寻找捣乱的睡鼠瑞可时，由莫莉带领发现了瑞可的家——一个黑漆漆的洞口，大家商议着如何要回被抢走的球。
[P6] 朋友们来到瑞可的家门前，贝琳达和弗雷迪用力敲门要求归还球，但无人应答。亨利认为可能没人在家，大家只能无奈地决定明天再来，越想越生气却毫无办法。
[P7] 朋友们在瑞可的家门前商议如何要回被抢走的球，有人提议找狐狸帮忙，有人主张明天自己拿回，而麦克斯则沉默地独自思考。
[P8] 第二天，麦克斯和朋友们再次来到睡鼠瑞可家门口，由莫莉和亨利敲门，向瑞可的妈妈索要被抢走的球，但对方生气地转身进洞并喊叫瑞可，朋友们只能愣在原地不知所措。
[P9] 朋友们在黑暗的走廊中发现被抢走的球滚了回来，大家兴奋地喊叫并抓住球，但麦克斯却停在原地，若有所思，似乎想到了什么办法。
[P10] 麦克斯将球扔进瑞可的洞穴后，球滚了回来，他邀请瑞可一起玩，但朋友们认为瑞可不会出来，球也拿不回来了，麦克斯却乐观地吹着口哨离开。
[P11] 瑞可从洞里出来，手里拿着球，麦克斯热情邀请他一起玩，并体贴地说明了朋友们各自的局限，希望他能加入游戏。
[P12] 瑞可同意当守门员，和朋友们一起开心地玩球，直到天黑，最后他接住球时，好奇地问起球的主人。
[P13] 麦克斯邀请瑞可一起玩球，并提出分享的理念，瑞可高兴地同意可以带球回家，大家达成共识，气氛融洽。
